# Codex fixture

`sessions/2026/09/05/rollout-2026-09-05T16-07-24-01a07365-0000-7000-8000-000000000001.jsonl` is a complete real Codex CLI 0.144.6 rollout (53 lines, three turns) captured 2026-09-05 on a laptop, redacted with the `redact-fixture` skill. The file name carries the local start time while every `timestamp` field is UTC, which is how Codex writes it. The session ran in the home directory, so its cwd is not a git repository.

Redacted: the `base_instructions` text, every developer, user, assistant, and `agent_message` text, tool inputs and outputs, reasoning `encrypted_content`, the web search query and action, `world_state` contents, and the prose inside the JSON-encoded `collaboration_mode` and permission settings, all replaced with `[redacted N lines]`; the cwd and workspace roots, replaced with `/home/fixture`; the session, turn, message, tool call, reasoning, and context window ids, replaced with stable fakes in the same format; the timezone. The `!` shell command on line 3 keeps its `<user_shell_command>` wrapper and the injected context lines keep their tag names so the rule that neither counts as a human turn can be tested.

Kept: every `type`, `payload.type`, `role`, `timestamp`, `cli_version`, `originator`, `source`, `model`, `model_provider`, `reasoning_effort`, `phase`, `status`, tool `name`, `internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough` shape, token counts, `model_context_window`, and every `rate_limits` snapshot with its `used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `resets_at`, `credits`, and `plan_type`.

Cases covered: `session_meta` with both `id` and `session_id`; `thread_settings_applied` carrying the model (twice); `turn_context` and `world_state` lines; three `user_message` events against six `response_item` user and developer lines that must not count; assistant messages with distinct ids; `custom_tool_call` and `custom_tool_call_output` lines (the reader counts `function_call` only, see `docs/testing/2026-09-06-local-run.md`); `web_search_end`; six `token_count` events whose `rate_limits` give twelve utilization samples on the `plus` plan; `task_started` and `task_complete` events.
